sections.h2: Where is Brighton, Colorado, and how big is it?
sections.html:
Brighton is a home rule city that sits in both Adams and Weld counties, and it is the county seat of Adams County. Most residents live on the Adams County side: 39,718 of the 40,083 people counted in 2020.

The city covers about 21.5 square miles at an elevation of 4,987 feet, and it belongs to the Denver-Aurora-Greeley area along the Front Range. For a seller, the split between two counties is the first practical detail, because the county decides who bills your property tax and who records your deed.

Brighton began as a stage and railroad depot and farming community called Hughes. The Hughes post office opened on April 13, 1871, and the name changed to Brighton on August 4, 1879, after Brighton Beach, New York.

The town was incorporated on September 1, 1887. Adams County was created on April 15, 1901, with Brighton as its seat. Brighton is therefore a county seat with more than a century of record keeping, and older parcels can carry older deed language that a title company will want to review.

sections.h2: What does Brighton's climate mean for a house?
sections.html:
Brighton has a cold semi-arid climate, so roofs, windows and heating systems get tested more by temperature swings and snow than by rain. Average annual precipitation is about 14.1 inches, and average snowfall is about 34.5 inches a year.

The mean daily high for the year is 65.5 degrees Fahrenheit and the mean daily low is 35.8. The record high is 105 and the record low is 26 below zero, set in December.

Buyers and inspectors in a climate like this tend to look hard at a few things:

  • Roof age and the condition of flashing and gutters
  • Furnace and water heater age
  • Window seals and attic insulation
  • Cracks in concrete and stucco from freeze and thaw

If your Brighton house has deferred work in any of these areas, a cash buyer who purchases as-is removes the need to fix them before closing.

sections.h2: What is Brighton's economy based on?
sections.html:
Brighton mixes manufacturing, retail and agriculture-related tourism. Two Vestas plants, a wind turbine blade factory and a nacelle plant, were valued at $290 million and provide 1,350 jobs, according to the published description of the plants.

The Prairie Center is a 396-acre shopping center with a pedestrian-oriented retail village. The Greater Brighton Chamber of Commerce has supported local businesses since 1955 and opened a Visitors Center in May 2020.

Yes. The census counted 40,083 residents in 2020, a 2024 estimate put the city at 43,473, and the Census Bureau estimate for July 1, 2025 is 45,395. The median age is 33.9 years.

Growth means more new construction competing with resale houses, and it also means more buyers and investors looking at existing homes across Adams County. A house that needs work may still draw interest from buyers who plan to renovate.

sections.h2: When are property taxes due in Brighton?
sections.html:
For Brighton properties in Adams County, you can pay in two halves or in one payment. The first half is due February 28, the second half June 15, and a full payment is due April 30.

Only half or full payments are accepted, and a bill of $25 or less cannot be split. Payments postmarked after a deadline pick up delinquent interest. Adams County says taxes are collected one year in arrears, which matters at closing: the tax bill you are asked to settle reflects last year's value and rates.

  • Delinquent notices are mailed in July.
  • Unpaid real property taxes are advertised before the online tax lien sale, which the county lists as running October 7 through November 6.
  • To avoid sale-related interest and fees, the county says to pay by 5:00 PM on October 31.

The Weld County portion of Brighton is billed by Weld County, so a seller with a Weld parcel should confirm dates with that treasurer. See the Adams County due dates page.

sections.h2: What repair work in Brighton needs a licensed contractor?
sections.html:
Brighton requires a city contractor license for general, mechanical, plumbing and electrical work, with an exception for owners working on their own home. The owner exception covers a personal residence and accessory buildings, and the city limits an owner to building one personal residence in three consecutive years.

Licenses are valid for twelve months, are not transferable, and require proof of liability insurance. Roofing, concrete flatwork, framing and drywall fall under the Class E specialty trades license. The city also lists a Minor Home Repairs Program and code enforcement under its Community Development pages.

This is useful when you are deciding whether to renovate before selling. Hiring a licensed contractor, pulling permits and passing inspections takes time, and the city notes that occupying a space before a certificate of occupancy can put a contractor's license at risk. Selling as-is avoids that process for you.

sections.h2: What do Brighton sellers usually run into?
sections.html:
Sellers in Brighton usually face a mix of timing, repairs and paperwork rather than one single problem. Common situations include:

  • An inherited house in Adams or Weld County that needs probate or a trust transfer first
  • Older roofs, furnaces or plumbing after decades of Front Range winters
  • A tenant in place and a lease that has to be handled
  • Back taxes or a mortgage that is behind

A traditional listing means showings, a buyer's inspection and a possible appraisal gap. A cash sale usually skips the lender, so closing can be scheduled around your date. Whichever route you choose, ask the title company for the Adams or Weld County tax figure before you set a closing date.

sections.h2: How does a cash sale work for a Brighton house?
sections.html:
A cash sale in Brighton follows the same basic steps as any Colorado sale, with the lender removed. The steps look like this:

  1. You tell us about the property, and we review it.
  2. We make a written offer based on the house as it stands.
  3. You choose a title company and a closing date.
  4. The deed is recorded with the county where the parcel sits, Adams or Weld.
  5. You receive the agreed proceeds at closing.

You can decline an offer and owe nothing, and you can compare it with a listing or an investor offer before deciding.

faqs.q: Which county do I deal with if I sell a house in Brighton, CO?
faqs.a: It depends on the parcel. Brighton sits in Adams and Weld counties, and most residents are on the Adams side, so most sellers deal with Adams County. Check your tax bill to see which county issues it.

faqs.q: When is the second-half property tax payment due in Brighton?
faqs.a: June 15 for Adams County parcels. The first half is due February 28, and the full payment is due April 30.

faqs.q: Do I need a contractor license to fix up my own Brighton house?
faqs.a: An owner working on a personal residence and its accessory buildings is excepted from the city's contractor license rule, though permits and inspections still apply. Hired contractors generally need a city license, and the city requires proof of insurance.
School District 27J serves the Brighton community.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Brighton house as-is?
faqs.a: Yes. A cash sale as-is means you do not have to repair or update the property for a buyer's lender or inspection. Ask for the offer in writing and review it with your title company.

faqs.q: Does the county tax bill change when I sell?
faqs.a: The bill follows the property, and Adams County collects taxes one year in arrears. The closing statement normally divides the tax between you and the buyer, so ask the title company how it was figured.
